issues.legal_issue: A writ petition challenging a completed state land-possession action may be denied when it is brought after a long, unexplained delay despite the petitioners’ prior knowledge of the action.
material_facts: The petitioners challenged a possession panchnama made in 1986 in a writ petition filed in 2001.

The State’s assertion that possession had been taken was recorded in proceedings in which the petitioners were involved by 1998, and compensation proceedings had also followed the taking of possession.
The petitioners did not explain the delay with a plausible reason; their explanation that they believed a deceased owner’s attorney was handling the matter did not justify the delay.
The petition sought to challenge the possession panchnama after the earlier proceedings had attained finality, without seeking broader relief concerning those proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The writ petition was hopelessly delayed and barred by laches, so the appeal was dismissed without deciding the parties’ other contentions on the merits.
issues.legal_principle: Relief under Article 226 of the Constitution is discretionary and equitable; delay and laches may defeat a claim, because equity favours a vigilant litigant rather than an indolent one. The Court relied on Shivgonda Anna Patil v. State of Maharashtra, AIR 1990 SC 2281, and Municipal Council, Ahmednagar v. Shah Hyder Beig, JT 1999 (10) SC 336.

rule.if: writ_challenge_to_state_possession and long_delay_after_possession_action and prior_knowledge_of_possession_action and no_plausible_explanation_for_delay

predicates.writ_challenge_to_state_possession: The petitioners brought a writ proceeding to challenge a state action taking possession of land.
predicates.long_delay_after_possession_action: The petitioners waited a long time after the possession action before bringing the challenge.
predicates.prior_knowledge_of_possession_action: The petitioners knew of the possession action before they brought the challenge.
predicates.no_plausible_explanation_for_delay: The petitioners did not provide a plausible explanation for waiting to bring the challenge.

issues.definition: When petitioners bring a writ challenge to a state possession action after a long delay, already knowing of the action and without a plausible explanation for the delay, the rule denies writ relief for laches.
